body:
# the contributor audit of the exact-replacement results

## Planar positive theorem

The proof in candidate 98181ddbde71e951 passes the
following independent checks.

- The elementary exposed-point density argument uses a scalar support
  function in a nonparallel normal chart. Differentiability fixes both planar
  coordinates of its maximizer, and the perturbation selects the desired
  endpoint of the original supporting segment.
- An extreme point of K intersect closure(R) in the open arrangement cell R
  would be extreme in K. Density would then supply an exposed point in R.
  Without such a point, all extreme points lie on finitely many cell walls;
  each wall contributes only the endpoints of one compact interval.
- Every resulting facet not supplied by a cell wall is a genuine supporting
  line of K. Adding those lines to an outer approximation fixes the entire
  cell, not only its area to first order.
- An exposed boundary point in an open cell has a compact shallow cap wholly
  in that cell. The same holds for sufficiently close outer approximations.
  Its removable volume is larger than the vanishing cell excess. Continuous
  threshold variation therefore removes precisely that excess. Different
  corrections have disjoint cells and cannot interfere.
- Empty, interior, and touching cells are separately handled. Arrangement
  lines have zero area, so exact open-cell areas give exact closed-cap areas.

This proves exact polygon replacement in ordinary dimension two. It does
not prove a mixed-fiber replacement theorem.

## General-dimensional obstruction

The proof in candidate 324b832a77b55308 also passes.

- Brunn--Minkowski equality applies to the positive full-dimensional unit
  slab bodies. Translation and midpoint equality force their full projection
  endpoints to be0 and3. Slice support functions after subtracting the shear
  are concave and periodic, hence constant. This gives an actual prism.
- Applying that rigidity in two slab coordinates eliminates cross-shears.
  Equivalently, a nonzero cross-shear would make the s-minimizing face of the
  first prism have dimension at most2, whereas the second prism has a
  three-dimensional facet there. The resulting double-prism representation
  retains all possible continuous shears and translations.
- Two tilted thresholds in each slab direction give independent equations:
  they first force its shear to vanish, and the other direction then forces
  the remaining shear and the planar centroid to vanish. Coordinate bounds
  ensure each affine threshold is interior to the integration interval.
- Each of the two corner caps integrates the polynomial
  (1/2)(1/2+epsilon x_i)^2. The measured coefficient101/800 at epsilon1/10
  forces each planar second moment to be pi/4.
- Area pi and total radial second moment pi/2 force the unit disk by the
  explicit nonnegative inside/outside comparison. Convexity upgrades equality
  almost everywhere to equality of the bodies themselves.

The exact coefficient verifier was run successfully. Thus twenty-two
halfspace volumes and total volume can uniquely determine a nonpolytope in
dimension four. General exact finite-cap polytope replacement is false.
The counterexample uses a centrally symmetric body and does not settle the
more restricted question for low-depth extremal cap certificates.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
